newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs say EU should stimulate renewable energy.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs say EU should stimulate renewable energy.

text.p: The European Union should do more to stimulate the use of renewable sources of energy, like biomass, wind, wave and solar power, the European Parliament said on Thursday.

In a report on the EU's energy policy white paper -- COM(95)682 -- parliament urged the European Commission and the EU member states to take practical action to increase the percentage of renewables in the energy mix.

This should include improving access for energy from renewable sources to the electricity grid, giving tax advantages to investments in renewables and dismantling subsidies on fossil fuels, the Euro-MPs said.

They warned of the increasing damage to the environment which fossil fuels were causing and criticised the Commission for not giving more importance in the white paper to biomass, especially as marketing biofuels could provide an alternative income for farmers.
Austrian Christian Democrat Agnes Schierhuber said using more biofuels was also essential it the EU was to get near its goal of cutting CO2 emissions to 1990 levels by the year 2000.

The parliament approved a second report on plans for cooperation in the energy sector with the countries of the Mediterranean Basin -- COM(96)149 -- which stressed the need for long-term plans to improve security of energy supply.

Signing an agreement to encourage the use of renewables -- especially solar power -- in the sunny Mediterranean countries, where demand for energy is soaring in line with economic growth, would be one way of doing this, parliament suggested.
The question of security of supply arose again when Euro-MPs discussed the Commission's communication on EU gas supply -- COM(95)487.
In a third report, the parliament noted that by 2010, the EU would be dependent on three third countries for nearly 60 percent of its gas needs -- Algeria, Russia and Norway.

Euro-MPs said it was necessary to guarantee these supplies would not be interrupted by means of a binding legal framework such as the pan-European Energy Charter Treaty, which imposes rules on such aspects as investment, transit and trade in energy.
The parliament urged the 50 signatories to the Energy Charter, which include the EU states and the countries of the former Soviet bloc, to ratify the legally binding treaty.
Another charter, which would bind the energy rich but unstable countries of the Mediterranean Basin to the same rules as its northern neighbours, should be the next step, Euro-MPs recommended.
